notes: nothing is read as a rule 35 fusion of כֹּל with לֹא; the partitive מִן before it is left unrepresented because one English word carries the universal and the negation but not the partitive relation (rule 40).
An alternative would give of to the privative מִן and leave כֹּל holding nothing alone; the fusion was taken because one English word answers to both morphemes.
The article on הַיַּיִן takes the phrase's single the, standing before its own word in the attributive rendering the grape vine (rules 28, 29).
